text: Fill in the correct AI application for each clinical laboratory scenario.
questions: When AI holds back a potassium result of 8.5 mmol/L in a well outpatient for human review because the value is implausible, this is *autoverification/auto-verification/auto verification:Think about what happens to each result before it is released to the ward.*.

Monitoring running averages of patient results to detect possible analyser drift, complementing conventional Westgard quality control rather than replacing it, is a *quality control/QC:This application monitors the measuring instrument's performance over time.* application.
Interpreting several analytes together to suggest a diagnosis is *pattern recognition:This application identifies diagnostic patterns across a set of test results.*.

Using serial results such as creatinine, potassium and lactate to warn the ward team of impending acute kidney injury or sepsis is called *predictive analytics:This application uses historical trends to look forward in time and anticipate clinical events.*.

overallFeedback.feedback: Each AI application serves a distinct laboratory function: autoverification validates individual results before release, quality control follows running averages of patient results and can detect possible analyser drift earlier than conventional Westgard QC for some analytes, complementing rather than replacing it, pattern recognition reads several analytes together to suggest a diagnosis, and predictive analytics follows serial results to warn of impending deterioration such as acute kidney injury — all require human oversight for unusual or novel cases.
